\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsmath, amsthm}
\newcommand{\bn}[1]{[#1]}
\newcommand{\fall}[2]{#1^{\underline{#2}}}
\newcommand{\Gf}{G(x)}
\DeclareMathOperator{\Chrom}{chr}
\def\NN{\mathbb{N}}
\newtheorem{thm}{Theorem}

\begin{document}

\begin{thm}\label{thm:gf}
Let $\NN$ be the natural numbers and $\bn{n} = \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$. The number
of injections $\bn{k} \to \bn{n}$ equals the falling factorial $\fall{n}{k}$,
with generating function $\Gf$. Moreover, $\Chrom(G) \le n$ for any graph $G$
on $\bn{n}$ vertices.
\end{thm}

\end{document}
